blindWork: n(SO2) = 1.00 × 10^6 g / 64.07 g/mol = 1.561 × 10^4 mol. The equation releases 198 kJ per 2 mol SO2, i.e., 99.0 kJ/mol. Heat = 1.561×10^4 × 99.0 = 1.55 × 10^6 kJ.
stem: Thermochemical Stoichiometry: Given: $2\text{SO}_{2}(g) + \text{O}_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_{3}(g)\quad\Delta H^{\circ} = - 198\text{~kJ/mol}$. How much heat is released when $1.00\text{~metric~ton}$ ($1.00 \times 10^{6}\text{~g}$) of $\text{SO}_{2}$ ($64.07\text{~g/mol}$) is converted to $\text{SO}_{3}$?
sourceExplanation: Moles $\text{SO}_{2} = 1.00 \times 10^{6}\text{~g}/64.07\text{~g/mol} = 15615\text{~mol}$. Heat released $= 15615 \times (198/2) = 1.55 \times 10^{6}\text{~kJ}$? Wait, $198\text{~kJ}$ per $2\text{~moles}$, so $15615 \times 99 = 1.55 \times 10^{6}\text{~kJ}$. Let's verify scaling. (B)
